correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs cleanly from the actual RESULT. Every selected point lies on one strictly convex circle, hence is extreme; equality of bodies therefore forces equality of the geometric parameter orbits. An affine equivalence sends the common circle to a conic with infinitely many points on the target circle, so the conics coincide and the affine map is a Euclidean circle isometry. Preserving the two accumulation points leaves exactly the parameter actions \(t\mapsto \pm t\) and \(t\mapsto \pm1/t\), giving \(y\equiv\pm x\pmod{2\eta}\). The area derivation from central-angle gaps is algebraically consistent; independent numerical evaluation at \(m=2\) reproduced \(A(0)=5.115775646069353\) and \(A(\eta)=4.966501630113537\), matching the record. Poisson summation and the standard Jacobi-\(\operatorname{dn}\) Fourier expansion then give the stated analytic law and strict monotonicity on the fundamental interval.
